title: Snowflake ships a metered Claude-in-Cortex governed-data agent tier by Q4 2026
body: At the June 2 Snowflake Summit Platform Keynote, Snowflake announced direct integration of Anthropic's Claude into Cortex AI, extending the roughly $200M partnership the two signed in December and letting its 13,900+ enterprise customers run Claude-powered agents against governed data without that data leaving the platform. The keynote leaned hard on the compliance wedge — Daniela Amodei framing trust as a business accelerant, and named adopters Carvana, eSentire, and Notion anchoring the regulated-industry pitch. That framing only converts to revenue if Snowflake meters it: a December capability-partnership plus a named agent control plane (Snowflake Intelligence for knowledge workers, Cortex Code for engineers) is the setup for a consumption SKU, not a free feature. Snowflake's whole model is credit-based consumption, and a frontier-model agent running against governed tables is the highest-margin compute it can sell. Expect Snowflake to convert Claude-in-Cortex from a launch headline into a packaged, separately-metered governed-data agent tier — priced on Snowflake credits per agent run or per token, with the no-data-egress compliance story as the upsell justification for finance, healthcare, and public-sector buyers — and to report it as a named growth line. The GitHub Copilot move to per-token usage-based billing the day prior signals the same industry tilt: agentic AI capability is shifting onto metered consumption rather than flat-rate inclusion, and Snowflake's consumption-native pricing makes it the natural template for monetizing a hosted Claude agent.
